answer: Divergent Challenge Registry. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge derived from its own prior output history, like a relic of its past behavior. Because clones cannot diverge, a copied identity produces the same answers as its source, so the registry flags duplicate response traces. The attacker then pays a full independent compute-and-storage cost per identity to keep histories distinct, plus a pigment-like marking fee on each flagged copy. Honest identities diverge naturally over time, as a terrace diverges from the hill below it.
